summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would amend existing financial legislation to support the DisabilityCare Australia Fund's operation, including state reimbursements and management by the Future Fund Board of Guardians.
It would enable reimbursements through the existing reform fund for state and territory grants and allow transfers between funds to apportion shared expenses.
The substantive amendments would start no earlier than 1 July 2014 and would depend on commencement of the companion Medicare levy increase legislation.
changes: The same investment manager could be engaged under the Future Fund, Nation Building Funds and disability fund arrangements.
The National Disability Insurance Minister would receive copies of relevant investment reports.
The Future Fund Board could delegate specified powers under the disability fund legislation.
Payments relating exclusively to the disability fund could not be debited from the Building Australia Fund.
summary.affected: State and territory governments, the Future Fund Board of Guardians and investment managers are affected.

speeches.speaker: Bernie Ripoll
speeches.brief: Proposed consequential amendments to establish the DisabilityCare Australia Fund, supporting the government's increase of the Medicare levy from 1.5 to two per cent of taxable income, and enabling the Future Fund to manage the fund and reimburse states through the COAG Reform Fund.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Robb
speeches.brief: Supported the DisabilityCare Australia Fund (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2013, which manages Medicare levy revenue raised by an increase from 1.4 to two per cent expected to reach $11.4 billion over the forward estimates and an estimated $20.4 billion by 2018-19, and said the coalition would establish a joint parliamentary committee to oversee the National Disability Insurance Scheme's implementation if elected.

speeches.speaker: Geoff Lyons
speeches.brief: Supported the DisabilityCare Australia Fund bill, saying 11,000 Tasmanians will receive support under the scheme, and drew parallels with Medicare, noting the Fraser government gutted Medibank in October 1976 before Labor reintroduced universal healthcare in 1984, and quoted the member for Warringah's 1995 description of compulsory superannuation as a con job to warn against a change of government.

speeches.speaker: Bernie Ripoll
speeches.brief: Moved to close debate on the DisabilityCare Australia Fund (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2013, saying support was necessary to provide certainty to the disability sector through transparent and accountable funding of the NDIS, and commended the bill to the House.
